case_title: Sanjeev Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P. (now State of Uttarakhand)
accused_victim_relationship: Political rival; prior dispute over withdrawing candidacy in a college election
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 read with s.149; IPC s.148
weapon: Lathis, knives, khukris (khukri used for neck and eye injuries); danda (stick) also used
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured eyewitness and corroborating eyewitnesses); medical; recovery (blood-stained shirt)
aggravating_circumstances: Accused armed with deadly weapons; deceased chased and attacked again by four accused after falling
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.149 and s.148 IPC; life imprisonment and Rs.10,000 fine each; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed under s.302 r/w s.149 and s.148; bail cancelled
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.149; rioting with deadly weapon under IPC s.148
neutral_facts: On a morning in September 1996, near a cycle stand inside a college campus, a group of seven accused, some armed with lathis, knives and khukris, approached two students standing there. They asked the victim and a second student to withdraw their names from a college election. When both refused, the accused assaulted them with their weapons. The victim was struck on the back, neck and face, then ran from the spot, became entangled in wire fencing near a nearby building, and fell. Several accused chased him there and attacked him again with sticks. The second student suffered a head injury. About three hundred students gathered. The victim was taken to hospital and died the next day. The second student lodged a written complaint at a police station, and the shirt he wore was seized. A medical officer examined both injured persons. The victim's frontal bone was found fractured and a lung ruptured; the second student's injuries were consistent with sticks. Eyewitnesses named all the accused and described their individual roles. One witness who had been present gave differing accounts to police and in court. The weapons were not recovered, and a blood-stained shirt was recovered six days after the incident.
physical_harm: Death of the victim (homicidal) from head and chest injuries; victim had knife and khukri wounds; second student had a lacerated head wound from a danda
number_of_offences: 4 charged (ss.147, 148, 302 r/w 149, and 323 r/w 149 for some accused); 2 finally upheld (s.302 r/w s.149 and s.148)
premeditation_planning: Not found; the Court held that the common intention to kill may have arisen on the spur of the moment
motive: Common object of stopping the deceased and others from contesting the college elections
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of injured P.W.1 and P.W.3 on presence and roles of all seven accused; medical evidence of injury reports and post-mortem findings; recovered shirt
witness_credibility: P.W.1 (injured eyewitness) found fully reliable; FIR-versus-court inconsistency not fatal due to possible post-incident trauma; no improvement found; P.W.4 turned hostile
bail_history: Bail cancelled by the High Court on affirming conviction; no other bail history stated
trial_duration: offence: 24.9.1996; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 08.04.2011; Supreme Court: not given
legal_representation: Appellants: K.T.S. Tulsi, R.S. Suri, A. Sharan and others. Respondent (State of Uttarakhand): Aditya Singh, Jatinder Kumar Bhatia, Gaurav Agrawal (AC) and others
investigation_status: FIR registered (Case Crime No. 275/96); charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Investigation flaws: weapon not recovered and blood-stained shirt recovered after six days; held not fatal
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced to life. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
defence_argument: Appellant Sanjeev Kumar Gupta not named in FIR and falsely implicated; varied accounts of number of attackers; eyewitness P.W.3 unreliable; place-of-occurrence discrepancy; no common object or intention to kill; no weapon recovered; no test identification parade
legal_principle_applied: Section 149 IPC: common object may form on the spur of the moment without prior concert; injured eyewitness testimony given much credence; minor discrepancies not fatal; non-recovery of weapon not fatal where medical and ocular evidence prove homicide
precedent_relied_upon: Dharmendrasinh alias Mansinh Ratansinh v. State of Gujarat (2002) 4 SCC 679; Manjit Singh v. State of Punjab (2013) 12 SCC 746; Ramachandran v. State of Kerala (2011) 9 SCC 257
other_sentence_order: None by the Supreme Court; trial court directed the sentences to run concurrently
